segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאַחִין שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֲבִיהֶם וִישֵׁנִים בְּבָתֵּיהֶם — צְרִיכִין עֵירוּב לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד. לְפִיכָךְ, אִם שָׁכַח אֶחָד מֵהֶם וְלֹא עֵירַב — מְבַטֵּל אֶת רְשׁוּתוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «brothers who were eating at their father’s table and sleeping in their» own «houses» in the same courtyard, a separate contribution to the «eiruv is required for each and every one» of them. «Therefore, if one of them forgot and did not» contribute to the «eiruv, he» must «renounce his rights» in the courtyard in order to render carrying in the courtyard permitted to the rest of the courtyard’s residents.

segments.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין עֵירוּבָן בִּמְקוֹם אַחֵר. אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵירוּב בָּא אֶצְלָן, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין עִמָּהֶן דָּיוֹרִין בֶּחָצֵר — אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְעָרֵב.
segments.en: «When» do they state this halakha? They state it «when they take their eiruv elsewhere» in the courtyard, i.e., to the house of one of the other residents. «But if the eiruv was coming to them,» i.e., if it was placed in their father’s house, «or if there are no» other «residents with» the brothers and their father «in the courtyard, they are not required to establish an eiruv,» as they are considered like a single individual living in a courtyard.

moves.cueHe: האחין שהיו אוכלין על שלחן אביהם
moves.summary: each brother needs an eiruv; one who forgot renounces his rights
only when the eiruv is taken elsewhere; not if it comes to them or there are no other residents

positions.claim: each brother needs his own eiruv; one who forgot renounces his rights; exempt if the eiruv comes to them or no other residents
